intro.title: Design Permission System
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple permission system for a web application using React. You will learn how to control what users can see and do based on their assigned roles, such as 'admin' or 'user'. The core concept is conditional rendering, where you use JavaScript logic to decide which UI components to display. You will work with React components, state, and props to create a dynamic interface that changes based on user permissions. This project will help you understand how to manage access control in a front-end application.
intro.usecase: Permission systems are fundamental to modern applications that manage user access and security. In enterprise dashboards, they control which data panels, analytics tools, and administrative menus different user roles can view or modify. E-commerce platforms use permissions to determine which staff members can update product listings, process refunds, or access customer data. Content management systems rely on granular permissions to allow editors, authors, and administrators different levels of content creation and publishing capabilities. As a developer, you'll implement these systems to ensure secure, role-based access across user interfaces.
